title: Obsidian sync MCP no-auth HTTP mode permits browser access to vaults
summary: Missing Host and Origin checks let a malicious website use DNS rebinding to read, create, edit, move and delete notes through the HTTP MCP endpoint.

severity.rationale: The documented no-auth local mode permits unauthorized vault access from a website. The impact is confined to the connected vault service.

exposure: The server must run without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN. Token-enabled deployments are not affected by the described browser attack. Filesystem and CouchDB-backed vaults share the vulnerable path.

params.instructions: Check obsidian-sync-mcp version and whether the documented exposure conditions apply.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to 0.5.7. Set MCP_AUTH_TOKEN on untrusted networks; Host and Origin checks alone do not authenticate non-browser clients.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed component uses the patched release and test the affected workflow with harmless inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
